title: How Many Different Numbers?

concept.title: The size of a set
body: Putting all numbers into a set removes the repeats, so the **size of the set** is the number of different values. Adding a value that is already in the set changes nothing.

In C++ `unordered_set<long long> s(a.begin(), a.end()); s.size()` does the same, and in Java `new HashSet<>(list).size()`. Because every number costs one insertion of O(1) on average, the whole count takes O(n).

statement: Count how many different values occur in a list of `n` integers.
outputFormat: Print the number of different values.
hints: Equal numbers should be counted once.
Insert every number into a set.
The answer is the size of the set.

explanation: A set keeps one copy of every value, so its size is the number of different values.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

distinct = set()
for x in a:
    distinct.add(x)
print(len(distinct))
